newsitem.title: CHINA: China province busts 3,801 suspected drug dealers.
newsitem.headline: China province busts 3,801 suspected drug dealers.

text.p: A three-month police crackdown on illegal drugs in China's southern province of Guangdong has netted 3,801 suspected dealers and 1,000 kg (2,200 lb) of narcotics, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Police had cracked 1,864 cases involving heroin dealing and smuggling and smashed 628 drug trafficking rings in a special anti-drug campaign from early April to mid-July, Xinhua said.
Anti-drug battlers had uncovered 33,600 drug addicts in the period, putting 28,000 of them into rehabilitation centres and forcing another 3,100 into labour camps, it said.

Drug use in China was nearly wiped out under the strict rule of former Chairman Mao Zedong but has surged in recent years as nearly two decades of economic reform erode the power of the state over people's lives.
China had 520,000 registered addicts in 1995, soaring from 148,000 in 1991, state media has said. Officials and analysts say the real number of people hooked on narcotics is much higher.

Guangdong is a main route for drug dealers moving their illicit goods to Hong Kong -- and onto the West -- from southwestern China and the major drug producing region of the "Golden Triangle" of Laos, Burma and Thailand.
